f: Class Proficiencies

A raveler is proficient with simple weapons, as well as light armor and bucklers. In addition, if this is this character’s first level in any class, they may select a martial tradition of their choice.
Casting

A raveler may combine spheres and talents to create magical effects. A raveler is considered a Mid-Caster. (Note: All casters gain 2 bonus talents and a casting tradition the first time they gain the casting class feature.)
Blended Training

A raveler gains a combat or magic talent every time they gain a class level. They also gain an additional bonus combat or magic talent at 2nd level, and every 2 levels thereafter. Ravelers use their casting ability modifier as their practitioner modifier.
Limited Pool

Unlike other spherecasters, a raveler does not innately gain a pool of spell points based on their class level and CAM. They can still gain spell points from other sources, as normal. If they take levels in another class that grants a spell pool, they add their CAM to their spell pool as normal. They can still gain spell points through other means, such as by taking drawbacks, and count as having a spell pool for the purposes of prerequisites, such as the Extra Spell Points feat.
Ravels (Su)

At 1st level, the raveler learns to weave the ambient forces of magic into a power known as ravels that grant them unique abilities or enhance them in a variety of ways. At 1st level, the raveler gains two ravels of their choice. At 5th level, and every 4 levels thereafter, the raveler gains 1 additional ravel of their choice.

Whenever the raveler gains a level, they can change one of their chosen ravels for another. Ravels can also be retrained as if they were a feat.

Ravels grant two different benefits that vary between constant effects to activated abilities known as woven effects and unwoven effects. By default, a ravel only grants its woven effect. When it is unwoven (usually by the raveler’s magicweaving or mightweaving class features), they instead gain the ravel’s unwoven effect. Ravels and the abilities they grant are supernatural effects unless described otherwise. The raveler uses their casting ability modifier to determine the effects of their ravels, known as their ravel modifier.

For more information on how ravels work and the descriptions of each ravel, see the ravel chapter of this book.
Magicweaving (Su)

Ravelers utilize a unique method of casting their spells, known as magicweaving, that fuels their magical power by unweaving their ravels. Whenever the raveler would be able to spend spell points on an effect or ability, they can unweave one of their ravels to immediately gain 1 temporary spell point to spend on that effect or ability. This spell point must be used as part of that effect or ability, or it is immediately lost. At 7th level, and again at 13th and 19th level, the raveler gains 1 additional temporary spell point when unweaving a ravel in this way. If the raveler starts casting a spell with a casting time longer than one full round, the raveler may unweave a ravel as they start casting the spell and invest those spell points into the effect. If they stop casting the spell early, those spell points are lost immediately.

If the raveler used these spell points to create an effect with a duration longer than instantaneous, that effect immediately ends if the ravel is no longer unwoven.
Mightweaving (Su)

Ravelers can also use the magical powers of their ravels to empower their martial abilities. Whenever the raveler uses an ability of a combat sphere, they can choose to unweave one of their ravels as part of using the effect. They can also unweave one of their ravels as a swift action to enhance the abilities of a continuous effect granted by a combat sphere. Unweaving one of their ravels briefly empowers that ability with their magic, allowing them to treat their Base Attack Bonus and skill ranks with that ability as 1 higher when determining the effects of that ability. This bonus further increases by 1 at 5th level, and every 4 levels thereafter.

For abilities with a duration or for constant abilities, this bonus lasts for the duration of the ability, or until the ravel is no longer unwoven (whichever happens first). If an item or object is created in this way (such as a Trap sphere trap or Alchemy sphere formulae), that created item is considered to be supernatural and is destroyed if the ravel stops being unwoven. This ability cannot be used with any ability that grants the raveler a companion, such as the Tame ability of the Beastmastery sphere.

For instantaneous abilities, this bonus applies every time that ability is used for as long as the ravel is unwoven, but no more than once each round.

If attacks are made as part of an ability affected by mightweaving, those attacks are not made using this increased base attack bonus (or increase in skill ranks, if the ability allows skill ranks to be used in place of base attack bonus). If skill checks are made as part of an ability affected by mightweaving, those skill checks are not made using this increase in effective skill ranks.
Combat Casting
At 3rd level, the raveler gains Combat Casting as a bonus feat. If they already have this feat, they gain a bonus feat of their choice instead.
Metaweaving
At 5th level, whenever the raveler casts a sphere effect using spell points gained from their magicweaving ability, any metamagic they apply to that sphere effect does not increase its casting time.
Bonus Feats

At 5th level, and again at 11th and 17th level, the raveler gains a bonus feat. Using these bonus feats may select combat feats, teamwork feats, ravel feats, Extra Magic Talent, drawback, proxy, and theurge feats, or any feat which has casting, a magic sphere, or a magic talent as a prerequisite (item creation feats, metamagic feats, Sphere Focus, Circle Casting, etc). They must still meet the prerequisites for these feats as normal.
Improved Combat Casting
At 9th level, the raveler increases the bonus provided by their Combat Casting feat by +4.
Greater Combat Casting
At 15th level, the raveler can choose to take 10 on concentration checks made to cast a spell or use a spell-like ability when casting defensively or while grappled.
Raveler’s Ascendance

At 20th level, the raveler’s mastery has reached its peak. Whenever one of their ravels is unweaved as part of their magicweaving or mightweaving abilities, the raveler maintains that ravel’s woven effect for the duration it is unweaved in addition to gaining its unwoven effect. It is still considered to be unwoven, and cannot be unweaved again until it has been recovered.

Additionally, ravels recover 1 minute after being unweaved instead of after 10 minutes. The raveler can still choose to extend this duration beyond 1 minute if they wish to continue the effects of an ongoing sphere effects cast using spell points gained from unweaving their ravel.

The card caster has developed a unique method of casting their spells, known as cardweaving, that involves unweaving a ravel to fuel the effects of their cards.

Once per turn as a free action (even outside of their turn) the card caster may unweave one of their ravels to gain 1 temporary spell point until the beginning of their next turn. At 7th level, and again at 13th and 19th level, the card caster gains 1 additional temporary spell point when unweaving a ravel in this way.

Whenever the card caster unweaves a ravel as part of cardweaving, they may choose to gain the benefits of an effect from **Table: Cardweaving Effects** in place of the normal unwoven effects granted by the ravel. If an effect has a prerequisite, the card caster must meet the prerequisite to choose that effect.

If the card caster unweaves a ravel outside of combat as part of using cardweaving and chooses to gain a cardweaving effect, they instead store that cardweaving effect instead of immediately gaining the benefits of it. If the triggering ravel is still unwoven when they next enter combat, at the start of combat after drawing their opening hand the stored effect is triggered. Additionally, when using this ability outside of combat they can unweave a ravel to gain temporary spell points after spending 1 minute to draw the card from their deck to use those temporary spell points to cast that card.

When the card caster uses the spell points granted by this ability on a sphere effect, that effect is tied to the ravel that granted those spell points. If such a sphere effect has a duration longer than 10 minutes (including sphere effects with a duration of permanent, but not sphere effects with an instantaneous effect), the card caster must choose whether to end the sphere effect after the ravel is no longer unwoven (normally after 10 minutes), or whether they leave it unwoven for the effect’s remaining duration. As a free action on their turn, the card caster can choose to end the duration of all effects tied to a ravel and return that ravel to its normal state (only after the initial 10 minutes has passed). If the ravel is restored to its normal state before this 10 minutes passes, any effects associated with it end at that time as well.

This modifies the raveler’s magicweaving class feature.

At 1st level, the dynamist gains the arcane reservoir and consume spells class features of an arcanist with the sphere arcanist archetype, using their casting ability modifier in place of their Intelligence modifier. The dynamist cannot use consume spells with temporary spell points gained from magicweaving.

In order to unweave one of their ravels, a dynamist must either spend an arcane pool point or increase the action taken to unweave the ravel by one step (swift action to move action, move action to standard action, standard action to full-round action). If the ravel is unwoven as part of taking another action, the dynamist must spend an immediate action to unweave the ravel.

Whenever the dynamist would be able to select a bonus feat or bonus talent from raveler levels, they may instead select an arcanist exploit, treating their levels in raveler as levels in sphere arcanist.

At 11th level, the dynamist may also select arcanist greater exploits in place of bonus feats or bonus talents.

Once per day, the guile raveler can spend 1 hour and choose a number of combat, magic or skill talents they do not possess equal to their operative modifier (minimum 1), plus 1 additional talent per 3 raveler levels after 4th, making these talents prepared. Once chosen, these talents cannot be changed until the raveler spends another 8 hours to change them. The raveler must possess the talent’s base sphere and must meet any prerequisites. If a talent offers a choice as part of gaining it, they make that choice when they prepare the talent.

Whenever a ravel is unwoven, the guile raveler can grant themself a single talent prepared with this ability for as long as the ravel remains unwoven. Whenever the guile raveler uses this ability again to select a new talent as part of unweaving another ravel, the guile raveler must replace a talent granted by a previous use.

At 6th level, the guile raveler can have up to two talents active at one time using their spontaneous technique ability, each corresponding to a different unwoven ravel. One of these talents can meet the prerequisites of the second talent; doing so means that the guile raveler cannot replace a talent currently fulfilling another’s prerequisite without also replacing the talents that require it.

At 8th level, the guile raveler can spend 1 minute to change one of the talents they have prepared using spontaneous technique, but cannot choose a [utility] talent when they use this option. The guile raveler may spend 1 use of skill leverage to instead change one prepared talent as a standard action.

At 10th level, whenever a ravel is unwoven, the guile raveler may unweave an additional ravel in place of gaining a prepared talent to grant a single combat, magic, or skill talent they have prepared with spontaneous technique to an ally within close range (25 feet + 5 feet per 2 class levels) for as long as both ravels are unwoven. The ally must meet the prerequisites for the granted talent, though the guile raveler is not required to do so. Any additional uses of this ability on a single ally ends the previous use. The guile raveler does not gain any talents from having either ravel unwoven in this way.

At 14th level, the guile raveler can have up to three talents active at one time using their spontaneous technique ability, each corresponding to a different unwoven ravel. In addition, the guile raveler may spend an immediate action to unweave a single ravel.

At 16th level, the guile raveler may unweave a ravel as a free action once per round and may spend an immediate action to unweave two ravels.

At 20th level, the guile raveler may gain the benefit of any number of selected talents with her spontaneous technique ability as a swift action. Each individual talent selected requires a ravel to be unwoven.

The ravelbound gains the dissonant heart, struggle, and strife class features of a dissident of their raveler level. Rather than using attunement steps as a dissident, a ravelbound’s current attunement is tied to the number of ravels they have woven or unwoven

  * While the ravelbound has all of their ravels woven, they are considered strongly attuned to one side of their struggle, chosen which this class feature is gained.
  * While the ravelbound has at least one ravel unwoven, but more ravels woven than unwoven, they are considered weakly attuned to the side of their struggle they would be attuned to while all of their ravels are woven.
  * While the ravelbound has an equal number of ravels woven and unwoven, they are considered unattuned.
  * While the ravelbound has more ravels unwoven than woven, they are considered weakly attuned to the opposite side of their struggle that they would be attuned to while all of their ravels are woven.
  * While the ravelbound has all ravels unwoven, they are considered strongly attuned to the opposite side of their struggle that they would be attuned to while all of their ravels are woven.

At 2nd level, the reality striker has learned to utilize their ability to weave and unweave magic offensively to unweave the very magic that makes up objects and creatures. The reality striker may use this ability in one of two ways, an unweaving burst or an unweaving strike.

**Unweaving Burst:** The reality striker fires a burst of unweaving energy as a standard action that provokes attacks of opportunity, making a ranged touch attack against a single creature or unattended object within Medium range (100 feet + 10 feet per level). The struck target takes damage equal to 1d6 + the higher of reality striker’s casting ability modifier or practitioner modifier. This damage increases by a further 1d6 at 5th level, and every 3 levels thereafter. Only the first d6 of damage is multiplied on a critical hit, and this damage ignores the struck targets damage reduction and resistances. This damage is not halved when dealing damage to objects, but is still affected by an object's hardness.

At 8th level, and again at 15th level, when the reality striker uses this ability they may fire an additional burst of energy. The second burst fired in this way suffers a -5 penalty to its attack roll, and the third ray fired suffers a -10 penalty to its attack roll.

**Unweaving Assault:** The reality striker infuses their weapon with energy that unweaves that which it strikes. As a standard action, the reality striker makes a single attack with a weapon they are wielding, dealing an additional 1d6 points of damage on a successful hit. This damage increases by a further 1d6 at 5th level, and every 3 levels thereafter. This damage is not multiplied on a critical hit, and ignores the struck target’s damage reduction and resistances. This additional damage is not halved when dealing damage to objects, but is still affected by an object's hardness.

At 8th level, and again at 15th level, when the reality striker uses this ability they may make an additional attack using their infused weapon. The second attack made in this way suffers a -5 penalty to its attack roll, and the third attack made in this way suffers a -10 penalty to its attack roll.

At 1st level, the specialist chooses a single combat or magic sphere in which to specialize in. If the specialist also has the casting raveler archetype they cannot choose a combat sphere, and if they have the martial raveler archetype they cannot choose a magic sphere.

If they choose a combat sphere, they gain the benefits of the conscript’s sphere specialization for the chosen combat sphere using their raveler level in place of their conscript level. Rather than using their conscript level to determine their effective base attack bonus or Hit Dice for that sphere, they instead treat their base attack bonus or Hit Dice as +1 higher when determining that sphere's effects. The specialist can choose sub-specializations for their chosen combat sphere if they wish to.

If they choose a magic sphere, they gain the benefits of the incanter’s sphere specialization for the chosen magic sphere using their raveler level in place of their incanter level. The specialist can choose sub-specializations for their chosen magic sphere if they wish.

At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the specialist gains a bonus talent from their selected sphere.

The specialist gains one fewer combat or magic talent at 1st level, and every 2 levels thereafter from their blended training class feature.

If they are a casting raveler, they instead gain one fewer magic talent from their magic talents class feature at those levels.

If they are a martial raveler, they are instead treated as a Proficient combatant when determining their combat talents granted by their combat training.
